spoken: Dhruv, what a performance in Vienna! Alcaraz took Medvedev down 6-4, 7-6. That second-set tiebreak was absolute domination at 7-2.

He got the break in game four, handed it straight back, then stayed composed. Medvedev double-faulted at 5-4 down to give Alcaraz the opening set. That secures Alcaraz a place in his fifth final of the year. Did you track his run earlier in the week?
Every minute. He had that wild 13-11 tiebreak against Nikoloz Basilashvili in a 6-1, 7-6 win, and then held off Tommy Paul 6-4, 7-6. Now he gets Alex de Minaur for the title.
Medvedev did not leave empty-handed either. Making the last four booked his spot for the ATP Finals in Turin. Now, out in New Zealand, the T20 series wrapped up with a thud in Hamilton.
A seven-wicket defeat stings, even if India won the series 3-2. Tim Seifert went berserk with 93 off 50 deliveries. How does our attack fail to defend 192 and let it go with two whole overs left?

Glenn Phillips took them apart at the death. His unbeaten 65 carried him to 341 runs across the series. That breaks Phil Salt's world record from 2023 for the most runs in any bilateral T20 series. India still set up a competitive 191 for eight first.

Ishan Kishan looked outstanding. Sixty-one off 32 balls with five sixes and five fours. That pushed him past Suryakumar Yadav's Indian record for the most T20 international runs in a single calendar year, getting to 1,220 runs. Plus he crossed the 2,000 career run mark in the format.

India also became the first team to reach 400 T20 international sixes in a single calendar year, clearing the rope 11 times. But Gautam Gambhir faced sharp scrutiny after leaving 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out for the fourth and fifth games.
Why bench the kid right after he hammered 45 off 19 balls?

Gambhir said directly that his job is to make the right decisions, not popular ones, stressing dressing-room security and continuity. Over in Mong Kok at the Hong Kong Sixes, India had a miserable run.

Nightmare stuff. Pakistan beat us by four wickets, then the UAE walked all over us by six wickets. We ended up in the 11th-place bowl play-off beating Bangladesh by five wickets just to finish 11th. Grim reading.

Over in Madrid, alarming news for Eder Militao. Thieves broke into his house through a third-floor bathroom window during the match against Barcelona, stealing watches, bags, and jewellery worth 391,000 dollars.
His family was on the ground floor watching the match! Horrifying to think what could have happened. What is Jose Mourinho planning on the pitch for Racing Santander?

Mourinho looks set to lock in his midfield balance, pairing Bernardo Silva and Aurelien Tchouameni as the double pivot. Tchouameni handles the defensive ball-winning while Bernardo provides the composure to advance play.
Did Mourinho have anything to say about the Kylian Mbappe China controversy?

He said often the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, but praised Mbappe for acting with class by apologizing quickly over his Mao Zedong comments. Off the pitch, Madrid feel confident of completing a January swoop for 16-year-old Manchester United talent JJ Gabriel, whose representatives are seeking an exit from England.
Now, Mexico City. Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson banging wheels in second practice was total madness. That stadium complex scrap was ridiculous.

Verstappen damaged his bargeboards through Turns 12 to 14. He called Lawson's defense not very smart behavior, asking why he would pick a fight with him. The stewards found their actions unacceptable and gave both drivers a one-place grid penalty.

What about qualifying, though? Lewis Hamilton grabbed his first Ferrari pole position! His first pole anywhere since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, beating George Russell by nine thousandths of a second.

At 41, Hamilton becomes the oldest polesitter since Mario Andretti at the 1982 Italian GP. Still in Mexico, Red Bull reserve Isack Hadjar was handed a formal warning for misconduct by the stewards after pushing an aggressive paddock guest seeking a selfie before opening practice.
Then in Basel, what happened to Novak Djokovic?

Jan-Lennard Struff snapped an eight-match losing slide against Djokovic, beating him 6-7, 7-5, 7-6 in the second round. Djokovic admitted the loss hurt, calling Struff's attacking precision something he had rarely faced. Struff then lost his semi-final to Jiri Lehecka, who now plays Valentin Vacherot in the Basel final.
And in Vienna, Alex de Minaur took down incoming world number one Alexander Zverev 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 to book his clash with Alcaraz.

In the NBA, the Golden State Warriors beat the Los Angeles Lakers 112-95. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg struggled badly after his war of words with Luka Doncic, logging six points, five turnovers, and fouling out at minus-20, but the team bailed him out. Steph Curry and Draymond Green are both rested for the Clippers clash.
And Cristiano Ronaldo rolled back the years! A 15-minute second-half hat-trick with goals in the 66th, 72nd, and 81st minutes to fire Al Nassr past Al Kholood 5-3.
Around the grounds. Afghanistan stunned Australia by four wickets in Mong Kok to claim the Hong Kong Sixes Cup final.
And in the Premier League, Manchester City were beaten 1-0 at home by Brighton.

spoken: What a chase in Auckland! I was genuinely nervous when Rohit Sharma got out for a duck off six balls. But Virat Kohli just took over.
He turns 38 tomorrow, and he looked completely in command. Seventy-four off fifty-one balls, with thirteen fours and a six.
That second-wicket partnership was pure class. Did you see how easily he and Shubman Gill handled the pressure?

They put on 113 runs. Gill played the anchor with 37, while Kohli pushed the scoring. New Zealand made 185, bowled out in 40.2 overs. Rain came down, the innings was cut to 32 overs, and India needed a DLS target of 143. India got home with five wickets in hand in 22.4 overs. Jacob Duffy took three for 49 to make it interesting, but India were always ahead.
And Kohli broke Sachin Tendulkar's all-time record! Most runs in ODI chases. That is staggering.

He now has 8,741 runs in chases, going past Sachin's 8,720. That comes at an average over 66. It was also his eightieth half-century in ODIs. Interestingly, Sachin was doing an AMA on Reddit this week, where he spoke about his own captaincy days in the nineties. He mentioned he didn't always have the freedom to pick his own team back then, though he praised how professional the BCCI is today.
And what about the ball in hand? Anshul Kamboj was brilliant, was he not?

He took Player of the Match with two for 22 in ten overs. After the game, he pointedly said one match does not decide a career, answering some of his critics. Also, people spotted Gill wearing a metallic gadget on his forehead called Temple. Kyle Jamieson even asked him about it. It turns out it is a fitness wearable from Zomato co-founder Deepinder Goyal.
India lead 1-0 in the five-match series. Now let's talk about Real Madrid. A clinical 3-0 away win at Racing Santander. Pure joy!

All three goals came in the first half. Mbappé scored an eleventh-minute penalty. Then Arda Güler set up Jude Bellingham in the twenty-first, and Yan Diomande smashed in a volley on thirty-six minutes.
Six straight wins in all competitions since the break! The momentum under Mourinho is sensational.

Though the referees' committee, the CTA, did admit that Mbappé's penalty should not have been awarded. As for the standings, Barcelona lead with 30 points, Atlético Madrid have 28, Real Madrid sit third on 27, and Real Betis have 23.
We are right on their heels. And how huge is this boardroom news? Rafael Nadal is joining Real Madrid's board of directors!

Yes, the 22-time Grand Slam champion will have his appointment ratified at the general assembly on November 21. Off the pitch, Madrid also have a verbal agreement to sign 16-year-old Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel in January. He walked out on United in September and has secured an EU passport.
And what did Jose say about Europe? Madrid are one of five teams with a perfect record.

Along with PSG, Aston Villa, Liverpool, and Betis. Mourinho brushed off early talk of winning the trophy, saying his priority is just locking down qualification points. For tonight's game against AEK Athens, Valverde is back and Vinicius can play because his ban is only domestic, while Güler and Tchouameni have been rested.
Now, Mexico City. Max Verstappen, take a bow! Starting fifth on the grid and taking the win!

His sixth win at that track. He joked afterwards that they should rename it the Maxico Grand Prix. Red Bull's strategy nailed it after a red flag set up a 25-lap dash, and Max mastered the slippery, low-downforce conditions to keep Lewis Hamilton behind him.
Lewis tried everything at the restart, but Max held his ground like a wall.

The bigger story in the title race is Kimi Antonelli finishing third. That officially makes the teenager the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. The standings now read Antonelli 380, Verstappen 261, Hamilton 259, George Russell 250, and Charles Leclerc 245.
And Carlos Alcaraz collected yet another trophy! He took down Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win Vienna.

That was his first Vienna crown, won without dropping a single set across five matches. He is now 16-0 in ATP 500 events this season, and 16-2 overall since returning from that four-month wrist injury.
His form is frightening. Speaking of grit, how about Novak Djokovic surviving his Paris Masters opener?

He had to dig deep. Djokovic beat Basel champion Valentin Vacherot 6-7, 7-5, 6-1. At 39, he became the oldest match winner in Paris Masters history, keeping his hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin alive where he sits eleventh in the race. He even had to take a medical timeout for his right shoulder early in that second set.
You can never count him out. Just like the Golden State Warriors! Two huge wins on the bounce.

They beat the Clippers 124-112 on Monday, with Steph Curry putting up 33 points, his third straight game scoring thirty or more. Then yesterday they edged the Phoenix Suns 116-113 to make it five wins in a row.
Though Draymond Green got tossed again! What went down there?

Two minutes into the second half, Green wrestled Suns center Khaman Maluach to the floor, then shoved Dillon Brooks in the neck during the scuffle. Two technicals and an automatic ejection. But Curry's clutch late steal helped close it out. Meanwhile, over at Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton called for serious internal talks after Charles Leclerc cut Turn 4 on the opening lap in Mexico, copping a five-second penalty that ultimately let Max through.
Tempers really boiling over in that garage. What is happening elsewhere?

The Oklahoma City Thunder announced they will retire Russell Westbrook's number zero on February 7, 2027, honoring his 18-year career and MVP legacy. On a somber note in Spain, FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono deactivated his social media following online abuse after an on-field collision that led to the tragic death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel from cardiac arrest. Teammate Lautaro Spatz publicly defended him, stating it was a purely accidental tragedy.

spoken: I was clutching my head watching Carlitos against Taylor Fritz. He lost the first set tiebreak 10-12, and then serving at 3-5 in the second set, Fritz had two match points to reach the semifinals and lock up his spot for Turin!
How did he survive those match points?

He saved both of them under tremendous pressure! Alcaraz said holding for 4-5 got the crowd standing up, and he used that energy to break back, take the second set 7-5, and race through the third 6-3.

That win puts Alcaraz into his first Paris Masters semifinal. He admitted afterwards that the feeling is unmatched. Earlier in the tournament, he beat Alex Michelsen 7-6, 6-3 in the second round, before getting a walkover in round three when Matteo Berrettini withdrew with an elbow injury.
So who does he face in the semifinals?

Casper Ruud, who defeated Nuno Borges 7-6, 6-4. Ruud noted he holds a 1-6 record against Alcaraz, with his lone victory coming at the 2024 ATP Finals. Ruud also mentioned having downtime after getting married during the grass season and recovering from a back injury sustained in Cincinnati.
Right, India in Wellington. Did anyone see this chase coming? India go 2-0 up in the five-match ODI series, winning by four runs on DLS, but seven wickets down chasing 134!
New Zealand were bowled out for 134 in 41 overs. Rain halted India's response at 113 for 7 in 26 overs. Young pacer Gurnoor Brar was Player of the Match, taking a career-best 4 for 30.

Brar was outstanding! He revealed he got plenty of inputs from Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Shubman Gill. His approach was simple: hit full lengths early on, then bring out the bouncer at the right moment.

Virat Kohli reached a major milestone during that chase. Needing just one run to surpass Ricky Ponting's 1,971 runs, Kohli hit a boundary to become the highest run-scorer against New Zealand in ODI history.

Pure greatness from Virat! Away from the pitch, bowling coach Morne Morkel paid tribute to Mohammed Shami following Shami's retirement from Test cricket. Morkel recalled how Shami helped him get familiar with the dressing room culture when he joined in 2024, and remembered sharing the squad during the 2025 Champions Trophy.

One administrative note: the first ODI between India and Sri Lanka on December 13 has been moved from Delhi to Visakhapatnam. The DDCA requested the change due to outfield renovation to a sand-based system and potential weather disruptions.

Now, Real Madrid in the Champions League! What an absolute roller-coaster in Athens! AEK Athens went 1-0 up in the 12th minute through Aboubakary Koita, assisted by Luka Jovic. Jude Bellingham leveled it on 32 minutes from a Marc Cucurella pass. But then Stavros Pilios put Athens ahead 2-1 in the 75th minute off another Koita assist! I thought our winning run was over!
Can Madrid keep this winning streak alive at Mestalla tonight?

Well, Kylian Mbappe equalised in the 78th minute from Denzel Dumfries, and Federico Valverde struck the winner in the 92nd minute off Brahim Diaz! A 3-2 victory! Koita was even sent off in the 95th minute. That extends Real's winning streak to seven matches across all competitions!

Off the pitch, Jude Bellingham was named Real Madrid's Player of the Month. Meanwhile, Chinese ambassador Yao Jing confirmed China and La Liga are maintaining communication following Kylian Mbappe's online comments regarding a meme of Mao Zedong, though formal apologies have been issued.
Looking to tonight's La Liga clash against Valencia, Vinicius Junior serves the final game of his four-match ban. Rodrygo, Ferland Mendy, and Raul Asencio remain sidelined with injuries.

Zinedine Zidane also commented on Mbappe's role for France in the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Italy and Turkiye, stating the forward will have total freedom to play in his preferred position.
And over in Formula 1 practice at Interlagos, Max Verstappen was absolutely livid! FP2 downshift issues triggered a furious radio rant to engineer Tom Hart, calling the downshifts unacceptable!
Will Max fix those downshift problems before qualifying?
I hope so! Max ended up third quickest in both sessions, behind P1 Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris.

Off the track, Verstappen offered newly crowned champion Antonelli some practical advice regarding post-title media demands, warning him that the commitments the next day are not nice, but you just deal with it.
Golden State make it six wins in a row! They beat the Miami Heat 120-100, and Steph Curry scored 29 points, passing Oscar Robertson on the NBA all-time scoring list!

There is sobering news for the Warriors, though. Center Kristaps Porzingis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health due to an undisclosed issue, noting his body did not respond as expected when ramping up.
In tennis, Novak Djokovic is officially out of the ATP Finals race after a shock second-round defeat in Paris, losing 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian Rinky Hijikata.
Did you expect Hijikata to pull that off?
Not after Novak dominated the first set! But despite that loss ending his 2026 season, Djokovic did break Roger Federer's historic longevity record earlier in the week.

Huge news from international football: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from the Portugal national team after 23 years. He finishes with 146 goals in 234 appearances, a Euro 2016 title, and two Nations League trophies.
That follows a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus after Ronaldo left training camp on his private jet last month.
In F1, Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara made his Haas debut at Interlagos, stepping in for Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the season. Camara finished P18 in FP1 and P16 in FP2.
Meanwhile, George Russell faces a five-place grid penalty for Sunday's race after Mercedes fitted his sixth internal combustion engine of the season.
Two quick tennis updates: Jannik Sinner confirmed his longtime coach Darren Cahill will depart at the end of the season.
And world No. 1 Alexander Zverev expressed sharp frustration over having to justify his top ranking after crashing out in his Paris opener to Lorenzo Musetti.

Around the grounds. In English amateur cricket, Saltburn player Brian Devine received a two-year ban for clicking his fingers to simulate the sound of an edge off the bat. Saltburn CC were relegated to division three, docked 60 points, and fined 300 pounds.
Unbelievable trickery! And in the Champions League, FC Porto comfortably beat Napoli 4-1.
